findings.claim: Across the full observed score window [0.0,0.49], the landmark_00 local displacement components show non-monotone, sign-changing trajectories: dx has 6 sign changes with 9 strong sign conflicts, dy has 6 sign changes with 4 strong sign conflicts, and dz has 10 sign changes with 7 strong sign conflicts, so no single monotone early-vs-late direction is supported for landmark 00.

landmark_00_soft_mass rises from a negative early level to a positive mid-window plateau and then declines toward the end (whole-window z=0.639, 4 sign changes, 1 strong sign conflict), indicating a mid-window occupancy/soft-mass emphasis rather than a monotone trend.

landmark_10 local displacement components are likewise non-monotone: dx has 6 sign changes with 13 strong sign conflicts, dy has 7 sign changes with 3 strong sign conflicts, and dz has 6 sign changes with 8 strong sign conflicts, with whole-window z near zero for dx and dz.

landmark_10_soft_mass shows an early rise to a positive plateau followed by a late decline (whole-window z=0.395, 4 sign changes, 2 strong sign conflicts), qualitatively similar in shape to landmark_00_soft_mass.

All eight read curves are flagged polynomial_accepted=false with relative_node_RMSE between roughly 0.29 and 0.83 and held-out batch MSE not improving with higher degree, so smooth low-order polynomial descriptions of these coordinate features are not supported over the observed window.

hypotheses.direction: increase mid-window dose weight, decrease early and late dose weight, keeping the same M2 scalar reward
hypotheses.falsifier: If the mid-window-weighted dose does not change the landmark_00_soft_mass mid-window elevation relative to the flat-dose control, or if the primary final affinity metric does not improve, the timing hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass z-profile over observed score nodes 0.0-0.49
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score-node window [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: For landmark_00_soft_mass, the observed profile is low early, elevated through the middle of the observed score window, and lower again near the end; a temporal dose recipe that shifts guidance weight toward the middle of the observed window (relative to a flat schedule) is worth testing against the fixed M2 reward geometry.

hypotheses.direction: increase mid-window dose weight, decrease early and late dose weight, keeping the same M2 scalar reward
hypotheses.falsifier: If the landmark_10_soft_mass mid-window elevation is unchanged relative to the flat-dose control, or if the primary final affinity metric does not improve, the timing hypothesis is not supported.
hypotheses.observable: landmark_10_soft_mass z-profile over observed score nodes 0.0-0.49
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score-node window [0.0,0.49]
hypotheses.statement: For landmark_10_soft_mass, the observed profile also rises early to a positive plateau and declines late; a temporal dose recipe emphasizing the middle of the observed window is worth testing as a second, independent landmark check of the same timing pattern.

limitations: Only landmark_00 and landmark_10 displacement and soft-mass curves were read; the remaining 192 catalogue features (including all local covariance components and landmarks 01-09, 11-19) are unqueried, so no whole-molecule temporal claim is made.
No stage profiles or temporal profiles are available; the analysis rests on continuous per-feature curves only.
Selection preference and coordinate associations are not evidence of descendant survival or measured final affinity benefit; no decoded final labels are present in this role input.
All read curves are non-polynomial (polynomial_accepted=false) with substantial node RMSE, so the described shapes are qualitative and should not be treated as fitted functional forms.
The observed soft-mass mid-window elevation is an association with the selection window, not a measured optimal guidance dose; the dose lane's registered recipes remain untested hypotheses.
